summary: This work presents a method for architecture-aware transpilation of general $n$-qubit unitary synthesis on superconducting quantum hardware, tightly integrating transpilation with the optimized block-ZXZ decomposition that uses $\Theta(4^n)$ CNOT gates. The method combines greedy qubit mapping, adaptive Gray code selection with qubit swapping, and CNOT-ladder heuristics to achieve 34–36% CNOT reductions versus Qiskit/Pennylane and 553× speedup versus TKET on 20-qubit IQM Garnet (square lattice) and 156-qubit IBM Marrakesh (heavy-hex) platforms for 3–11 qubits.
motivation: Exact synthesis of general unitaries is essential in Hamiltonian simulation, quantum state preparation, QSP/QSVT, and block-encoding subroutines, but existing transpilers treat synthesis and routing as decoupled steps, losing opportunity to exploit the recursive structure of block-ZXZ decomposition for hardware-specific optimization.
method: Architecture-aware transpilation integrates three techniques: (1) greedy qubit mapping minimizing pairwise distance cost $C_{\mathrm{dist}} = \sum_{u,v \in S} d(u,v)$ on the coupling graph; (2) adaptive selection of cyclic Gray codes that assign highest CNOT frequencies $f_{n-1} = 2^{n-2}$ to physically nearby qubits, combined with SWAP optimization; (3) a heuristic exploiting intermediate entanglement in long-range CNOT ladders (requiring $4k-4$ gates for distance $k > 1$) to opportunistically apply $R_z$ gates and merge redundant CNOTs.
result: On IQM Garnet, average CNOT reductions of 27% versus Qiskit and 36% versus Pennylane; on IBM Marrakesh, 19% versus Qiskit and 34% versus Pennylane. Transpilation times scale as $O(|V|^2 + |V| \cdot n + n^2 \cdot 2^n)$, achieving 553× speedup over TKET and enabling successful transpilation of 11-qubit unitaries within 30 minutes where TKET and Pennylane failed beyond 8 qubits. CNOT counts exceed the theoretical lower bound by 44% (IQM Garnet) and 58% (IBM Marrakesh) due to routing overhead.
